title: DENSE_RANK vs RANK — Tied Salaries
description: Compare RANK() and DENSE_RANK() when ranking employees with tied salaries.

data.text: Write a query showing both RANK() and DENSE_RANK() side by side for employees ordered by salary, highlighting the difference when ties exist.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
SELECT
    EmployeeID,
    FirstName,
    LastName,
    Salary,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS RankVal,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS DenseRankVal
FROM Employees
ORDER BY Salary DESC;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: With salaries [100k, 90k, 90k, 80k]: RANK gives [1, 2, 2, 4] (gap after ties); DENSE_RANK gives [1, 2, 2, 3] (no gaps). Use DENSE_RANK when you want consecutive ranks. ROW_NUMBER would give [1, 2, 3, 4] — no ties allowed.
